name: co.quantkit/asia-market-mcp
title: Asia Market Data
description: A-share/HK/US data: unofficial, may be delayed, for information only — not financial advice.

tools.name: stock_quote
tools.description:
Get the latest available quote (price, change, day range, volume) for one stock in a single market.

Reads from free public feeds (Tencent for A-share/HK, yfinance for US);
no API keys involved. Data is unofficial and may be delayed; where the
response has a "timestamp" field it shows when the quote is from. Invalid
or unknown symbols return an {"error": ...} object instead of raising.

Use this for ONE symbol. Use stock_quote_batch when the request names
multiple symbols — it returns one call's worth of data for up to 20 at
once. Use kline instead for historical bars, market_summary for index
snapshots. This tool is read-only and safe to call repeatedly.
Requires no authentication.

symbol.description:
Stock symbol in CODE.MARKET format — market is one of
SH (Shanghai), SZ (Shenzhen), HK (Hong Kong), US (US listings).
Examples: "600519.SH", "0700.HK", "NVDA.US". HK codes may omit
leading zeros ("0700.HK" == "00700.HK").

tools.name: stock_quote_batch
tools.description:
Get latest available quotes for up to 20 stocks in one call, in symbol order.

Same data and sources as stock_quote, just batched: each list element is
one quote object (or an {"error": ...} object for that symbol — one bad
symbol never fails the batch). No API keys involved; data is unofficial
and may be delayed.

Use this when a request mentions MORE THAN ONE stock, and stock_quote
when it names exactly one — results are identical per symbol, so the
batch simply saves round-trips. Requests naming more than 20 symbols
are truncated at 20 and the response includes a "note" saying how many
were skipped. Read-only and safe to call repeatedly.

symbols.description:
Comma-separated CODE.MARKET symbols, e.g.
"600519.SH,0700.HK,AAPL.US". Whitespace around commas is fine.

tools.name: kline
tools.description:
Get historical daily K-line (candlestick/OHLCV) bars for one stock.

Returns daily bars only — this tool never returns intraday ticks; for the
latest available price use stock_quote. A-share and HK bars come from the
Tencent public feed (forward-adjusted where the feed provides it, which is
not guaranteed for HK); US bars come from yfinance. Newer dates last. No
authentication required.

Use this when the request is about history: trends, ranges, chart data
over days-to-a-year. For the latest price alone use stock_quote (much
faster); for market-wide indices use market_summary. Read-only.

symbol.description:
Stock symbol in CODE.MARKET format — SH, SZ, HK, or US
(e.g. "600519.SH", "0700.HK", "AAPL.US"). HK codes may omit
leading zeros.

period.description:
Lookback window ending today: "1mo", "3mo", "6mo", or "1y".
Defaults to "3mo". For A-share and HK symbols any other value
returns an error. Each bar has date, open, close, high, low,
volume.

tools.name: market_status
tools.description:
Report open/closed state for US, HK, and CN stock markets right now (US also pre-market/after-hours).

Calculated from a built-in unofficial schedule against the current clock;
no data feed is contacted. US hours follow New York time, daylight saving
included. Markets are shown closed on listed exchange holidays (US and HK
2026-2027, CN 2026); US early closes end at 13:00 and HK half days at
12:00. For a year without a calendar the response carries a "warnings"
entry. Lunch breaks and unscheduled closures are not modelled. Read-only,
instant, no authentication.

Use this to check whether a market can trade before quoting; use
market_summary for index prices, stock_quote for individual stocks.

tools.name: market_summary
tools.description:
Get the latest price and day-change percentage for six major global indices (S&P 500, NASDAQ, Dow Jones, Hang Seng, SSE Composite, CSI 300).

Sources are public feeds (yfinance); values are the latest available,
unofficial and possibly delayed. An index that fails to fetch returns an
"error" entry for that index only.
Read-only, no authentication.

Use this for market-direction questions spanning regions; use
stock_quote for single stocks, kline for index history, and
market_status for open/closed state.
